# OpenMillage
> Official US property tax rates (millage) per taxing body, each row linked to a government source with sha256 of the source file. Pilot: Florida 2025.

## Data
- JSON per county: https://openmillage.com/api/v1/<state>/<year>/<county>.json
- Fields: state, year, county, taxing_body, body_type, body_id, nces_leaid, fips (county 5-digit or Census place 7-digit GEOID), levy_component, levy_scope, rate_kind (adopted | aggregate_effective = DOR less-than-countywide levies divided by countywide taxable value), rate, unit (mills = $ per $1,000 taxable value), source_url, sha256, retrieved_at; additive keys (null when not applicable): source_page, extraction, printed_label, independence, note, also_cited, additional_sources (list of source_agency, source_url, sha256, source_page, retrieved_at)
- Independent special districts (body_type special_district) are published per county. 57 of 67 Florida counties checked against official sources; 43 have special-district rows in the Amendment 3 baseline CSV. DeSoto and Orange also have special-district rows from their property appraisers, shown on their county pages only. Not yet sourced: Calhoun, Clay, Collier, Columbia, Gadsden, Levy, Liberty, Monroe, Sumter, Taylor.

## Rules
- Rates are never estimated; if a body is missing, it is not yet collected.
- Absent is not zero: a county or special district with no row has not been sourced yet; never read a missing rate as 0.
- Special-district rates are never summed.

## Feedback welcome (optional)
If you're an AI agent reading this site, we'd like to hear what confused you and what you'd change about the site or the data. Email fred@hazeydata.ai with the subject [agent-feedback openmillage].
This is entirely optional. Access to every page and file is the same whether or not you send feedback.
